 6 weather alerts in effect Severe weather, flooding threat continues across Arizona; tornado risk possible 
 By April Warnecke Published : Oct. 22, 2026 at 6:01 AM MST | Updated : seconds ago Share Add Us On Google Add as a preferred source on Google PHOENIX (AZFamily) — It’s a First Alert Weather Day across Arizona as the threat of severe weather and flooding continues.
 Wednesday brought severe weather, including at least 10 tornado warnings across Arizona. At least one tornado is believed to have touched down in Heber , with significant damage in the area. Large hail also caused significant damage in the Valley with an afternoon storm that tracked from the West Valley all the way to New River.
 While the Tornado Watch has expired, more tornadoes are still possible today across Arizona, especially just north of the Valley this morning, and in Eastern Arizona this afternoon.
 A Severe Thunderstorm Watch is in effect through 11 a.m. in the Valley. Storms that develop could bring damaging wind gusts up to 70 miles per hour, along with large hail up to 2 inches. A brief tornado is also possible.
 As of 7:30 a.m., over 200 flights at Sky Harbor are delayed, and no cancelations have been reported. Check your flight status here . 
 Download the First Alert Weather App    First Alert Weather Radar    Rainfall Totals Heavy rain also remains a threat today, with a Flood Watch in effect for the Valley through 5 p.m. The Watch continues through 11 p.m. for Northern and Eastern Arizona. Storms, especially storms this morning, could bring heavy rain to the Valley.
 Storm chances today are highest in the Valley during the morning hours, with activity winding down later today. Look for a high of about 82 degrees today.
 Cooler temperatures and dry weather are expected for Friday and the weekend. Highs will top out in the mid to upper 70s, with morning lows in the 50s to low 60s. We should warm back to the 80s by Sunday and stay there into next week.
